sentences.text: Rivian went from no revenue in FY2019 [F1] to $5,387 million in FY2025 [F7], a 48.1% three-year CAGR from FY2022 [D342].
The step change was FY2022, when revenue jumped 2914.5% [D83] on deliveries of 19,412 vehicles [P67], and FY2023 added another 167.4% [D135].
Growth then decelerated sharply to 12.1% in FY2024 [D187] and 8.4% in FY2025 [D239].
FY2025 revenue growth came despite Automotive revenue falling 14.6% [D315], as deliveries dropped 9,332 vehicles partly on the expiration of 45W tax credits [P22].
In FY2025 Software and Services contributed 21.6pp of the 8.4% revenue growth [D323][D239], with segment revenue up 221.7% to $1,557 million [D322][S26].
That increase came primarily from vehicle electrical architecture and software development services, remarketing, and repair and maintenance [P18].
Automotive, still 71.1% of revenue [D314], subtracted 13.2pp [D316], and New electric vehicles fell 12.5% [D287].
Operating expenses grew 6.9% against revenue growth of 8.4% [D258][D239], so incremental operating margin was 264.7% [D265].
Diluted shares rose 17.1% [D260], so EPS improved 34.5% [D242] while net loss shrank 23.2% [D241].
Gross margin turned positive at 2.7% in FY2025 [F19], against a window median of -45.8% [D332] and a FY2021 low of -845.5% [D330].
Operating margin of -66.5% [F31] is the window high but still far below the peer median of -1.6% [D344].
The FY2025 operating margin improved 27.8pp [D253], almost entirely from cost of revenue, which fell to 97.3% of revenue [D220] and added 26.8pp [D267].

Automotive cost of revenue fell on fewer vehicles produced and lower raw material, component and conversion costs [P21], and Automotive gross losses improved on higher average selling prices and lower cost per vehicle [P20].
SG&A cost 0.5pp of margin [D269] as go-to-market expansion raised payroll, stock-based compensation and facilities expenses [P13].
Operating cash flow was -$779 million in FY2025 [F64], or -14.5% of revenue [D227], against a net loss of $3,646 million [F38].
The improvement in operating cash use was primarily driven by a significant reduction in net loss [P4].
Free cash flow was -$2,489 million [F78], a -46.2% margin [D226] versus a window median of -132.9% [D335].
Capex rose 49.9% to $1,710 million [D246][F71], 31.7% of revenue [D225] and 2.18x D&A [D228], on Normal Factory capacity expansion [P3].
Net cash fell to $1,642 million in FY2025 [D231] from $3,259 million in FY2024 [D179], as cash and investments dropped 21.0% [D261].
Net cash is still 30.5% of revenue [D232], above the peer median of 17.8% [D352] and the 75th percentile of four autos peers [D351].
Financing brought in $886 million [F92], primarily from $750 million of Class A shares issued to Volkswagen Group [P2].
Total debt held at $4,440 million [D230], and the current ratio fell to 2.33x [F129], the window low [D339].
Rivian has posted a net loss in each of the last seven years [R1], including $3,646 million in FY2025 [F38].
Stock-based compensation was 13.8% of revenue in FY2025 [D223] and at least 10% in each of the last five years [R2], equal to 20.7% of the operating loss [D237].
Cash and investments of $6,082 million [D229] cover 2.4 years of the latest burn [D236][R3].
New electric vehicles were 67.6% of revenue and fell 12.5% in FY2025 [D286][D287][R4], and Automotive fell 14.6% [D315][R5].
Product revenue members sum to 129% of consolidated revenue in FY2025, so segment figures should not be added [R6].
Whether gross margin holds above the FY2025 level of 2.7% [F19] or slips back toward the -24.1% of FY2024 [F18], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether operating cash flow improves past the FY2025 -$779 million [F64] toward breakeven, or reverses from the FY2024 -$1,716 million [F63].
Whether net cash stays above the FY2025 $1,642 million [D231] as capex runs at 31.7% of revenue [D225], or falls toward the FY2024 $3,259 million [D179] trajectory.
